messages:
rafael_sales: Heads up on the Zephyr POC— AzureAD SAML setup failing and SCIM group pushes are erroring out. Customer says SSO is "blocked" for their pilots. Need quick help.

meera_se: What errors are they seeing in the SAML flow? Screenshot/trace helpful. Is this SP-initiated or IdP-initiated?

rafael_sales: IdP-initiated. Azure shows: `NameID value not in expected format (urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:unspecified)`. They mapped NameID -> user.mail in the assignment claims. On our side ACS accepted but our authn code expects emailAddress format.

akshat_eng: That mismatch will fail at validation. Two quick options: 1) change Azure claim to send `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress` as NameID/emailAddress, 2) relax SP NameID format check to accept unspecified and parse from `AttributeStatement` `mail` attribute. Which is easier given POC?

rafael_sales: Customer prefers minimal changes on their side. Which is safer on our end for POC?

meera_se: Safer: accept unspecified for POC and read mail attribute as fallback. We'll add a temporary flag in tenant config `saml.nameid_fallback=true`. Dev, can you patch?

akshat_eng: Pushed a small middleware: if NameID format != emailAddress, look for AttributeStatement[mail] or claim `email`. Deployed to canary at 18:12 and to staging. Need a rollback plan if something weird shows up.

idp_bot: SAML-processor: received POST from 40.112.72.5, relayState present, NameID format=urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:unspecified, assertion valid=false, reason=NameID parsing error

meera_se: OK after canary deploy try again. Also SCIM group provisioning: customer reports 409 on POST /Groups with payload that includes `displayName` and `members` as objects. Our SCIM service replies: `409 Conflict: group already exists with externalId` but they didn't set externalId.

akshat_eng: We are treating a incoming `displayName` collisions as conflict if SCIM schema `externalId` is missing to avoid duplicates. Azure AD sends group pushes without `externalId` by default. For POC we can either: A) accept `displayName` idempotency for dedicated POC (risky), B) instruct them to set "Immutable ID"->externalId mapping in Azure AD provisioning (recommended), C) accept Azure's `id` field as externalId if present.

rafael_sales: Will ask them to add mapping. But they want a quick workaround so pilot can continue.

meera_se: Quick temporary workaround: enable `scim.accept_azure_id_as_external=true` for their tenant. That will use Azure's `id` field (a GUID) as our externalId if externalId missing. Apply via Console > Tenants > Zephyr > Features (POC toggle).

dave_prod: Note: when enabling that flag we also need to ensure our logs redact GUIDs in traces. I pushed a log-filter change to staging. Also remind: if they move to Dedicated we must add clause to onboarding doc about configuring Azure mappings and provisioning connector docs.

akshat_eng: Ran tests: with nameid_fallback + scim.accept_azure_id_as_external toggles, saml post now validated and group push returns 201. Test curl for SCIM group upsert:
```
TOKEN=pcpoc-token
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://private.zephyr.redwood-company.com/scim/v2/Groups -d '{"displayName":"eng-team","members":[{"value":"user-123"}] }'
```
Expect 201 with group resource and externalId set to Azure id.

rafael_sales: Customer executed test and says both SSO and provisioning now work. They want confirmation that dedicated deployment will require different steps re certs/VPC egress.

meera_se: Yes: Dedicated onboarding requires (1) explicit Azure provisioning mappings (externalId or ImmutableID), (2) SAML NameID format agreement (emailAddress preferred), (3) allowlist of our egress IPs for SCIM callbacks or static NAT in their VPC, (4) TLS cert for tenant domain if using private callback. We'll send checklist.

dave_prod: I'll attach the POC checklist and a short playbook for enabling the two POC toggles and the rollback steps. Also adding pricing note: tenant customizations in Dedicated fall under enterprise onboarding (SOW), not covered by standard POC.

rafael_sales: Perfect — I'll close the loop with Zephyr and update the deal thread. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
